withdrawn.summary: The result previously published on this page for its primary outcome was a cardiovascular-death-only registry measure served as the composite outcome. It is withdrawn.
statements: What was published: EMPEROR-Preserved (NCT03057951, PMID 34449189), HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.09), p=0.30 -- ClinicalTrials.gov measure 'Time to Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death', a component of the composite, served as the review's k=1 primary result; a null-crossing conclusion.

What the held evidence holds: the registered PRIMARY composite (ClinicalTrials.gov measure #1, 'Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure', randomised set) reports HR 0.79 (95.03% CI 0.69 to 0.90), p=0.0003 -- the interval is alpha-adjusted at 95.03% for the interim analyses. This is quoted as what the source holds; it is NOT stated here as this review's result.

Why: the declared component set for 'Composite cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure' was ['cardiovascular death'] -- the topic declared no components, so the target was the vocabulary's reading of the title -- and a cardiovascular-death-only registry measure matched a cardiovascular-death target with missing_components empty and was classified EXACT_TARGET. A wrong target, matched faithfully.
The correct result was in the held registry data (cache/empagliflozin-hfpef-hosp/records.json, ctgov_results) throughout.

The corrected estimate is not yet published: registry analysis selection by identity and the confidence-level fix (the 95.03% level travels with the analysis instead of being rendered as 95%) must land first. Replacing a wrong number with a right number carrying a wrongly-labelled interval is not a correction.
Provenance: found by an independent verifier panel while measuring the cost of strict endpoint binding -- the rule refused this row, a true positive; confirmed against the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API.
withdrawn.status: Pooled estimate withheld until the corrected selection is served with its own correction record.
